hints.FailedGetResourceMetric: The metrics API (metrics.k8s.io) is not installed: install metrics-server, or remove the HPA.
hints.FailedComputeMetricsReplicas: The HPA can't read its metrics: install metrics-server, or check the HPA's metric names.
hints.FailedScheduling: No node fits the pod: check its requests, node selectors, taints and free capacity.
hints.FailedMount: A volume couldn't be mounted: check the Secret, ConfigMap or PVC it refers to.
hints.FailedAttachVolume: The volume couldn't attach: it may still be attached to another node.
hints.Unhealthy: A probe is failing: check the probe's path and port, and the app's startup time.
hints.BackOff: The container keeps exiting: open the pod for its last exit code and logs.
hints.ErrImagePull: The image couldn't be pulled: check the image name, tag and registry credentials.
hints.ImagePullBackOff: The image couldn't be pulled: check the image name, tag and registry credentials.
hints.FailedCreatePodSandBox: The pod's network couldn't be set up: check the CNI plugin on that node.
hints.Evicted: The node ran short of memory or disk and evicted the pod.
hints.OOMKilling: The kernel killed a process for memory: raise the memory limit or find the leak.
hints.FailedToCreateEndpoint: An Endpoints object with this name already exists: usually harmless after a Service is re-created.
hints.ClusterIPNotAllocated: Kubernetes repaired a Service's cluster IP: usually harmless.
hints.DNSConfigForming: The node's resolv.conf has too many search domains or nameservers.
hints.NodeNotReady: The node stopped reporting: check the kubelet and the node's network.

auth_failed.reference: Check the password in the Secret or the file, then Check now.

fix.permission_missing: Grant {missing} to {user}, or use the read-only user WatchLog creates. Then Check now.
fix.unreachable: Check that {service} runs, and that the integrations collector runs where it can reach it ({host}).
fix.login_untested: Logging in is checked once WatchLog reads {service} itself. Until then this test only shows that the port answers.

postgres.permission_missing: Grant it as an admin: GRANT pg_monitor TO {user};

redis.permission_missing: Add the commands to its ACL as an admin: ACL SETUSER {user} {missing}

settings.title: Settings · {name}
settings.noAccess: No password stored: WatchLog connects without one.
settings.pausedHint: The collector stops reading it; its history and alerts stay.
settings.removeConfirm: Stop monitoring {name}? Its stored access and its alert rules are removed too; its history stays until it ages out.

add.title: Add a service
add.description: One the agents can't see, such as a managed database, by its address.
add.addressHint: host:port, as the collector reaches it
add.hostHint: The host whose integrations collector reaches this address.
add.name: Name (optional)

reasons.evicting: Keys are being evicted: {n} in the last 15 minutes. Writes push out old data.
reasons.no_maxmemory: No maxmemory is set: memory can grow until the container's limit, and then it is OOM-killed.
reasons.slow_keys_command: KEYS appears in the slow log ({n}×): it blocks the server while it walks every key. Use SCAN.
reasons.replica_down: A replica is disconnected from its primary.
reasons.save_failed: The last save to disk failed: a restart would lose data written since.
reasons.clients_rejected: {n} connections were refused in the last 15 minutes: maxclients is reached.
reasons.clients_blocked: {n} clients are blocked waiting (BLPOP, XREAD, WAIT…).

page.generic: WatchLog checks that its collector reaches every member of this {service} and how fast it connects. The {service} pages (memory, commands, keys and the rest) come with its integration.

notFound.title: Service not found
notFound.description: It may have been removed from monitoring.

connected.from: From the service map (eBPF), no setup needed.
connected.none: Nothing connected to it in this time range.
connected.noFlows: Network flows are off for this cluster, so WatchLog can't see who connects.

mcp.title: Your AI can read this too
mcp.body: Through MCP, with the same reasons:

page.startCollectorHint: Run this on that host. It reuses the token of the WatchLog agent already running there, reads with read-only access, and mounts /etc/watchlog/secrets read-only for passwords you keep in files.

panel.empty: No data yet in this time range.
panel.needsPermission: WatchLog's user can't read this yet.

alerts.title: Alerts for this service
alerts.none: No rules for this service yet.
alerts.error: Its alert rules couldn't be loaded.
alerts.anyMetric: Any metric on this page can be used in a rule.

panels.slowlogNote: normalised: command and key prefix, no values
panels.prefixesNote: estimated from a sample of key names every 10 min
panels.lagNote: bytes behind the primary; Redis has no lag in seconds

memory.capacity: Add {missing} to the user's ACL to read maxmemory and its policy.
memory.prefixes: Add {missing} to the user's ACL (key names only; values are never read).

roles.locked: Viewers can't change this. Ask an Admin.

users.title: Users
users.intro: People who can open this WatchLog. Their role decides what they can change. API tokens follow the role of the person who made them.
users.viewerBanner: You're a Viewer: you can see everything here but not change it.
users.viewerAsk: To add someone or change a role, ask an Admin, for example {email}.
users.smtpBanner: Email isn't set up, so invites and password resets are shared as links you copy and send yourself.
users.setUpSmtpToSend: Set up SMTP to send these by email →
users.ownAccount: Change your password with a reset link from an Admin

owner.name: Owner
owner.desc: Whoever installed WatchLog, until they hand it over.
items: +Reset their own password from the command line if locked out

admin.name: Admin
admin.desc: For the people who run the clusters.
items: +Invite Admins and Viewers, change their roles

viewer.name: Viewer
viewer.desc: For people who need to look, not change.
items: +See every cluster, service, alert and the service map
+Make personal read-only API tokens for MCP

audit.invite_renewed: Made a new invite link for {subject}

users.inviteDescription: They choose their own name and password when they open the link.
users.emailHint: Used to sign in. Nothing is sent to it unless email is set up.

inviteRole.admin: Changes alert rules, channels and integrations; can invite others.
inviteRole.viewer: Sees everything, changes nothing. Good for most of the team.

users.oneOwner: There is one Owner. You can hand ownership to an Admin later from their row.
users.inviteHowSmtp: Email is set up: WatchLog emails the invite and also shows you the link.
users.inviteHowLink: Email isn't set up: you'll get a link to send yourself. It works once and expires in 7 days.

link.inviteFoot: You can copy the link again, or revoke it, from their row while it is pending.
link.resetFoot: {name}'s current password keeps working until a new one is set. Resetting signs them out everywhere.
link.notEmailed: Email isn't set up, so nothing was sent. Share this link yourself, in Slack, chat or wherever your team talks.

users.removeSignedOut: They lose access right away and are signed out.
users.removeTokens: They have no API tokens. | Their API token is revoked, so their AI assistant and scripts stop working. | Their {n} API tokens are revoked, so their AI assistant and scripts stop working.
users.removeStays: Alert rules, silences and connected services they set up stay, and keep working.
users.ownerBody: {name} becomes the Owner and can hand ownership over or delete clusters. {owner} becomes an Admin. There is one Owner at a time.

invite.title: Join WatchLog
invite.name: Your name
invite.foot: This link works once and expires on {date}. If you didn't expect it, you can ignore it.
invite.expiredIntro: Invite links work once and for 7 days. Ask {who} for a new one: it takes them one click.
invite.unusableIntro: It has been used or revoked. Ask whoever invited you for a new one.
invite.signIn: Already have an account? Sign in

reset.title: Set a new password
reset.intro: For {email}. Your current password keeps working until you set a new one.
reset.foot: Setting it signs this account out everywhere else.
reset.used: It has been used. Ask an Admin for a new one, or use Forgot your password? on the sign-in page.
reset.expired: Reset links work once and for one hour. Ask an Admin for a new one, or use Forgot your password? on the sign-in page.
